title: Agent configuration
description: Declarative definition of a voice/chat agent. A generic runtime loads this at call start and builds the agents, tasks and tools from it. Custom keywords: 'x-ref' names a collection of ids declared elsewhere in the same document (the UI renders a dropdown of them; validate_config.py rejects dangling ids), 'x-ui' carries form-widget hints. TEMPLATES: any string may contain {{path}} placeholders. Roots: state, args (tool arguments), result (tool response), const, meta (id, name, version), call (id, room, dnis, started_at, ended_at, duration_s, transcript, summary), channel (id, type, modality), caller (id), pbx (host, port, transport), target (a transfer's resolved target), with (extra variables from a notify action), form (submitted fields), plus the loop variable named by '$each'. Filters: {{x | format('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','Asia/Singapore')}}, truncate(n), upper, lower, default('x'), or(path) (fall back to another value, e.g. state.ttf_session_id | or(call.room)), join(', '), urlencode, map('user=IN','assistant=OUT'). A JSON object {"$each": "call.transcript", "as": "m", "do": {...}} inside a body expands to an array with one expanded 'do' per item (items of call.transcript carry role, text, index and at (when the message was committed); tool calls are not included and items with empty text are skipped).

schema_version.description: 1.2 adds, all optionally: sensitive state variables, the collect_dtmf action, typed task steps (collect / call / say) with store_in, requires, per-step attempts and on_exhausted, task chaining (on_*.next), and post_call.redaction. A config that uses any of them must say 1.2; the validator checks. Every 1.1 config is also a valid 1.2 config once its version says so.

version.description: Semantic version. Publishing creates an immutable version; the runtime loads id@version or id@published.

provider_mode.description: plugins = your own provider keys (works self-hosted); inference = LiveKit Inference (Cloud only). One config targets one mode: model names differ between them.

dispatch_name.description: Deprecated and ignored: the generic runtime is one worker pool for every bot, and a call names its bot in dispatch metadata ({"bot": id, "ref": "production"}). Kept so older configs still validate; omit it in new ones.

secrets_vault.description: Which vault the { "secret": NAME } references resolve against.

timezone.description: Default IANA timezone for spoken times and date formatting.

http_port.description: Health/drain endpoint. Give each agent on a host its own.

num_idle_processes.description: Warm worker processes. Lower on shared/small hosts.

delete_room_on_close.description: Deleting the room hangs up the SIP leg / disconnects the widget when the session ends.

drain.description: Let closing speech finish playing before the line is dropped.

constants.title: Constants
constants.description: Fixed values referenced as {{const.name}} (payment URLs, thresholds, wording variables). Not secrets.

sources.description: Tried in order; the first that yields a value wins.

strip.description: Regexes removed from the identity, e.g. ^sip[:_] and @.*$.

default_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Applied with libphonenumber rules (trunk prefixes, calling code).

host.description: Referenced as {{pbx.host}} in transfer URI templates.

dnis.description: Dialled number this bot answers; recorded with call logs.

defaults.title: Defaults (inherited by every agent and channel)

speaks.description: Languages the bot answers in. Every message with per-language text should cover these.

connection.description: Per-component API retry policy. SDK defaults: 3 retries, 2s apart, 10s timeout.

max_unrecoverable_errors.description: Consecutive unrecoverable STT/LLM/TTS errors before the session is closed.

on_session_error.description: Runs as the session closes after unrecoverable errors. Speech cannot finish at that point (the close does not drain, and the TTS may be the failing part), so only a pre-recorded sound, a webhook or a log line are allowed.

messages.title: Messages (everything the bot says verbatim)
messages.description: A catalogue of fixed lines, referenced as { "message": id } wherever speech is accepted. Text may be one string or per-language; per-language entries must include the primary language.

state.title: Session state
state.description: Typed per-call variables that tools read and write and that conditions/guardrails refer to. Replaces a hand-written session dataclass.

tasks.title: Tasks (scoped sub-conversations that return a result)

connections.title: Connections (define once, reference from tools and events)

wrapups.title: Wrap-ups (single-shot 'close if no reply' after a natural end point)

on.description: state_changed runs once for each state variable whose value changed; use `when` with {"event": "variable", "equals": "intent"} plus state conditions to pick the case. Hooks that themselves change state can trigger further state_changed hooks, up to a built-in limit.

redaction.title: Redaction of what is saved or sent
redaction.description: Sensitive text is replaced before a transcript or metrics file is written, before `call.transcript` is used in an API call or an email attachment, and in logs and traces. It does not change what the model hears during the call: keep PINs and card numbers out of the conversation by taking them as keypad digits. Schema 1.2.

entities.description: Kinds of value to find and replace.

patterns.description: Extra regular expressions whose matches are replaced.

mask_sensitive_state.description: Also mask the exact value of every `sensitive` state variable wherever it appears.

artifacts.description: Per-session files or payloads written when the session ends (any shutdown reason).

log_llm_requests.description: Record full model requests (everything sent to the model, every turn). The runtime writes them to the call's session log, as `session_log.detail: full` does. Logs conversation content; keep off in production.

session_log.title: Per-call event log
session_log.description: One file per call in the bot's own folder, written as the call runs (a call that crashes still leaves its file): what the caller said, each model request, every tool call with arguments, result and duration, every API call (status and time), state changes, handoffs, transfers, forms, notifications, inactivity nudges, errors and a closing summary with model usage. On by default. It records what callers say; `sensitive` state variables are masked, but redaction of free speech is not applied yet.

directory.description: Folder name inside the bot's own folder. It cannot be an absolute path or contain `..`.

detail.description: `events` = what happened. `full` adds every model request in full and the query, request body and response of every API call. Keep `full` for testing.

retention_days.description: Delete this bot's session files older than this many days. Checked when a call starts, at most once an hour. If it is not set, files are kept, unless whoever runs the workers sets AGENT_RUNTIME_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS as a default for every bot. Transcripts and metrics files are not covered.

endpoint.description: OTLP HTTP collector, e.g. a self-hosted SigNoz.

said_matches.description: Some assistant message matches this regex.

judge.description: Natural-language criterion graded by an LLM.

secretRef.title: Secret reference
secretRef.description: Credentials are never stored in the config; only a name resolved from the vault at runtime.

lookupValue.title: Value, secret or lookup
lookupValue.description: A literal, a secret, or a value chosen from a state variable: { "lookup": { "state": "intent", "map": { "sales": ..., "support": ... }, "default": ... } }.

recipients.description: One or several addresses/numbers (templates allowed), a secret, or a lookup by state.

speech.title: Speech
speech.description: Literal text, or a reference into the messages catalogue.

fallbacks.description: Tried in order if the primary provider fails.

keyterms.description: Words the recogniser should favour (brand names, jargon).

tool_calling.description: False for models without function calling (some self-hosted ones). Agents on such a model cannot have tools; use knowledge mode 'inject'.

vision.description: True if the model accepts images. The builder rejects image inputs unless the effective model has this set.

realtimeConfig.title: Realtime (speech-to-speech) model
realtimeConfig.description: Replaces the llm for the agent that uses it. With modalities ["text"] the model only produces text and the agent's tts speaks it, so the voice stays the same across agents.

probability.description: Chance this clip is chosen when the cue fires.

pronunciationRule.title: Pronunciation rule
pronunciationRule.description: Applied in order to the text sent to TTS (never to the chat transcript). The text is buffered to a clause boundary first, so '4:30' and 'PM' arriving in different chunks are handled together.

pattern.description: Matches are read character by character (e.g. TK100901 -> T K 1 0 0 9 0 1).

plus_prefix.description: Spoken form of a leading +, e.g. 'plus '.

symbols.description: Symbols or codes that introduce an amount, e.g. ["$","USD"].

conversation.title: Conversation behaviour
conversation.description: Same shape in defaults, per channel and per agent: objects merge key by key, arrays replace.

min_delay.description: Seconds of silence before the turn can end.

mode.description: adaptive needs LiveKit Cloud; use vad when self-hosted.

max_tool_steps.description: Maximum consecutive tool calls per LLM turn.

inactivity.title: Inactivity (away) handling
inactivity.description: Nudge a silent caller a bounded number of times, then run on_exhausted. The count resets whenever the caller does something real. Closing speech is played out in full (drain) before any hangup.

clock.description: silence = caller AND bot silent for timeout_s, paused while a tool runs (the SDK's away state); user_activity = timeout_s since the caller's last message, bot output ignored. auto = silence on audio channels, user_activity on text.

max_nudges.description: Nudges before on_exhausted. 0 = go straight to on_exhausted.

nudges.description: Nudge n uses nudges[n-1]; the last one repeats.

thinking.description: Played while the agent is thinking (LLM/tool calls), so a slow turn is not dead air. One clip is picked by probability each time.

ambient.description: Looped background sound for the whole call (e.g. office ambience).

max_hold_chars.description: Longest text held while waiting for a clause boundary.

model.description: auto = telephony model for SIP callers, standard otherwise. LiveKit Cloud only.

modelOverrides.description: Per-component override. null switches that component off (e.g. no tts on a text channel); an object is merged over the default.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.description: Same shape at every level (agent, channel): only what differs from the defaults.

sensitive.description: A PIN, one-time code, card number or similar. The value is never shown to the model, never put in a prompt, spoken line or log message, and is masked out of saved transcripts, metrics and traces. It can be used only inside API requests and notifications ({{state.pin}} in an http body). The validator refuses it anywhere else. Schema 1.2.

source.description: How the runtime fills the variable when the call starts. Omit for variables only tools and tasks set.

channel.description: modality resolves to 'voice' when the channel outputs audio, otherwise 'chat'.

kind.description: epoch_hex = epoch seconds plus 4 random hex characters.

end.description: Exclusive. 24:00 = end of day; 00:00-24:00 on all seven days is 24/7.

holidays.description: Closed all day. Wins over overrides.

overrides.description: One-off exceptions to the weekly pattern, by date.

comparison.description: Comparison operators shared by every condition that tests a value. At least one is required.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: Tests one thing (state, tool argument, tool result, channel, schedule) or combines conditions with all / any / not.

arg.description: Name of an argument of the tool being run.

event.description: Name of a detail of the event that is running this hook: handoff (from, to), tool_error (tool, error), state_changed (variable, previous, value), transfer_succeeded / transfer_failed (transfer, target, reason), inactivity (nudges).

instructions.description: The model writes the reply from these instructions. Costs an LLM call and fails if the LLM does; prefer say for must-deliver lines.

to_state.description: Store parts of the response in state. This is how a call_started hook preloads who the caller is from their caller ID (a screen pop) before anyone speaks.

skip_when_empty.description: Skip the request when this template value is empty (e.g. don't post a transcript for a call with no speech).

actionCollectDtmf.title: Collect keypad digits
actionCollectDtmf.description: Ask for digits on the phone keypad and keep them in a state variable. The digits never pass through speech recognition, the model, the transcript or the logs, which is how a PIN, OTP or card number should be taken. Mark `into` as a sensitive variable. Needs a phone channel. Schema 1.2.

into.description: The state variable that receives the digits as text.

num_digits.description: Stop as soon as this many digits are in.

timeout_s.description: Give up after this long with no key pressed.

terminator.description: A key that ends the entry early, usually #.

prompt.description: Spoken before listening (for example 'Please enter your new PIN, then press hash').

on_timeout.description: Run when nothing was entered in time, instead of continuing.

action.title: Action
action.description: One step run by an event, a tool effect, a transfer, a form submission, a notification failure, a wrap-up or inactivity.

result_to_state.description: Record the outcome so later prompts can use it (e.g. 'the confirmation was sent by {{state.x}}').

sent_by.description: Which delivery worked: the 'via' connection id.

transfer.title: Transfer to a person or queue

method.description: sip_refer = blind SIP REFER of the caller's existing leg; http_request = ask an external bridge to move the session (e.g. into a skill queue).

target.description: sip_refer: a number or SIP URI, or a lookup (e.g. by intent).

uri_template.description: A template: how a bare number becomes a SIP URI (it may also append URI parameters, e.g. ;sip_h_X-Reason={{args.reason | urlencode}}). Targets that already start with sip: or tel: pass through unchanged.

body.description: Template; may use {{target}} for the resolved target (a skill id, say).

schedule.description: Only transfer while this schedule is open; otherwise run 'closed'.

before.description: Run first (e.g. register the call as 'transferring' in a platform DB).

delay_s.description: Wait after 'before' so the registration lands before the transfer is attempted.

strategy.description: first_success = try the entries in order and stop at the first that works (email, then SMS).

content_type.description: How an email body is sent. Ignored for SMS.

otherwise.description: Run instead when the channel cannot show a form (a phone call): typically say what to do, or hand over to an agent that asks for the details in conversation.

wrapup.title: Wrap-up
wrapup.description: Started by a 'wrapup' action at a natural end point (a tool just finished the job). Waits wait_s for any reply; if none comes, runs on_silence. Deterministic: not an LLM judgement, and separate from session-wide inactivity.

match.description: How the runtime decides a connecting participant belongs to this channel. Defaults follow the type (sip_voice = SIP participants).

entry.description: How traffic reaches this channel; the fields depend on the type. Unknown keys are allowed for custom channels. These fields describe the route and are not read by the runtime: a call reaches a bot through the SIP dispatch rule for its number, or the session token for a web widget, both of which name the bot and environment. Setting `dnis` here does not connect a number.

inputs.description: Details for the non-text inputs listed in modalities.input.

topic.description: Byte-stream topic the client sends uploads on.

on_receive.description: reply = the bot starts a reply as soon as the image arrives; attach = it waits and attaches the image to the caller's next message.

human_transfer.description: False = a transfer_or_callback tool skips the transfer on this channel and runs its fallback straight away.

forms.description: Can this channel show a form? Default: true for web_chat and web_voice, false for the rest. Where it is false, a form runs its `otherwise` actions instead.

instructions_append.description: Appended to every agent's prompt on this channel (e.g. 'the caller has no camera').

mode.description: turn_attach = the latest camera frame (or uploaded image) is attached to each caller turn; any vision-capable llm works. continuous = frames stream into a realtime model that can speak unprompted; needs a realtime model.

max_dimension.description: Longest side in pixels sent to the model.

watch.description: continuous only. A realtime model does not react to new frames by itself, so the runtime samples frames, diffs them cheaply, and nudges the model only when the picture visibly changed.

change_threshold.description: Mean per-sample difference (0-255) that counts as a visible change.

kind.description: router = front door that only hands off; specialist = does one job; standalone = single-agent bot.

opening.description: Extra instruction applied once when the agent takes over.

conditional.description: Extra instruction added only while a condition holds (e.g. 'the caller is not verified yet').

knowledge.description: Knowledge bases in 'inject' mode retrieved for this agent on every caller turn. (Mode 'tool' bases are reached through a knowledge tool instead.)

description.description: Tells the LLM when to take this handoff.

set_state.description: State recorded when this handoff is taken, e.g. the caller's intent for later routing.

announce.description: Spoken while the handoff happens (covers a slow start).

on_enter.description: Actions run, in order, every time this agent takes over (on the entry agent, after the channel greeting): say a fixed line, show a form, send a notification, set state. If one hands off or ends the call, the rest are skipped. Defining on_enter hands the agent's entry to you: the model then speaks first only if `opening` is also set (a handed-over agent without on_enter always replies on its own).

channels.description: Restrict this agent to these channels. Omit for all.

use_prior_context.description: Give the task the calling agent's conversation so it uses what the caller already said instead of asking again.

steps.description: The stages of the task, in order. A step is offered only when its `requires` holds, and later steps cannot be reached before earlier ones have passed: the runtime enforces this, not the model.

max_attempts.description: Failed answers allowed per step before it gives up, unless the step sets its own.

inactivity.description: Override the session inactivity policy while this task runs (e.g. longer while a caller looks for an account number).

taskStep.title: Task step
taskStep.description: One stage of a task. `collect` (the default) asks the caller for one value and checks it; `call` runs actions (an API call) without asking anything; `say` speaks a fixed line. Steps written the 1.1 way, with only id, ask, skip_if and validate, are collect steps and unchanged.

ask.description: collect: what the model asks for.

input.description: collect: how the caller answers. dtmf = keypad tones taken straight into `store_in`, never seen by the model or written to the transcript: use it for a PIN, OTP or card number. Needs a phone channel. Schema 1.2.

store_in.description: collect: the state variable that receives the answer once it has passed `validate`. Mark it `sensitive` for a PIN, OTP or card number. Schema 1.2.

do.description: call and say: the actions to run, for example an http action that stores its answer with to_state. Schema 1.2.

pass_when.description: call: the step has passed when this holds after its actions ran (for example the API answered ok). Omit it and the step passes unless an action failed. Schema 1.2.

requires.description: The step is available only once this holds. Put what must already have succeeded here (identity_verified): it is checked in code. Schema 1.2.

skip_if.description: Skip this step when the condition holds, e.g. the account is already identified.

validate.description: How the answer is checked. A tool decides in code, so the model cannot talk its way past it.

args.description: Arguments for the tool as templates; {{value}} is the answer just given (and other state is available). Needed for a keypad answer, which the model never sees; for a spoken answer the model supplies the arguments when this is left out. Schema 1.2.

max_attempts.description: Attempts allowed on this step. Overrides the task's max_attempts. Schema 1.2.

on_exhausted.description: Run when the attempts are used up, typically a transfer or a handoff; then the task's on_failure applies. Schema 1.2.

resume.description: caller = the agent that started the task.

silent.description: True = the task says nothing on completion and the caller agent carries on.

next.description: Start this task next instead of returning to the caller: a chain such as verify, then OTP, then set the PIN. Schema 1.2.

do.description: Actions run when the task ends this way (a transfer after a failure, a notification after success). Schema 1.2.

name.description: The name the LLM sees; defaults to id. Two tools may share a name only if their channels do not overlap: a voice variant and a chat variant of the same tool.

description.description: Shown to the LLM; says when to use the tool.

channels.description: Only offered on these channels. Omit for all.

reply.description: model = after the tool runs, the model answers using its result. none = nothing more is said by the model this turn: use it when the tool's effects already spoke or showed something (a form, a transfer), so the model does not talk over it.

effects.description: Run in order after the tool succeeds, each when its condition holds. This is where 'say a fixed line then hang up', 'set the call outcome', or 'hand off on chat only' live, in config rather than in code.

tool_error.description: Returned to the LLM instead of running the tool.

say.description: Spoken in full, then the line is dropped. Done in code so the goodbye is never skipped.

fallback.description: Runs when the transfer cannot happen (no target, closed hours, REFER failed): say a callback line, raise a ticket.

pending_request_into.description: Adds an argument where the agent records what the caller still needs, stored in this state variable for the entry agent to pick up ({{state.NAME}} in its instructions). The runtime clears it after the entry agent's first reply.

guard_loops.description: Refuse to return unless the caller has spoken since this agent's last tool call. Stops the router and a specialist handing the caller back and forth in a loop.

digits.description: Fixed digits; omit to let the model choose.

into.description: Keep the digits in this state variable and tell the model only that they were collected. Without it the digits are returned to the model: never do that for a PIN, OTP or card number. Schema 1.2.

builtin.description: noop does nothing itself; only its effects run (set state, hand off). Use it for a tool whose whole job is a conditional handoff.

parameters.description: JSON Schema of the arguments the LLM supplies; mainly for noop. Available to effects as {{args.NAME}}.
JSON Schema of the arguments the LLM supplies. Referenced in templates as {{args.NAME}}.

to_llm.description: Only these response fields are shown to the LLM; everything else is dropped.

out_of_band.description: Response fields delivered straight to the caller (SMS/email) without ever passing through the LLM.

count_attempts_in.description: State variable incremented on each call to this tool.

allow.description: Explicit allow-list of the server's tools; nothing else is exposed.

handler.description: Reference to the function, e.g. tools/lookup.py:run.

auth.description: Provider credentials, each a secret reference (e.g. tenant_id, client_id, client_secret for microsoft_graph).

mode.description: tool = the model decides when to search (needs tool calling); inject = retrieve on every caller turn and add the chunks to the prompt (works without tool calling).

top_k.description: Chunks retrieved per query. Raise it when topics are split across many small files.

guardrails.title: Guardrails
guardrails.description: 'enforcement' says how a rule is applied: prompt = instruction to the model (soft), code = checked by the runtime (hard), both = prompt plus a code check. Detectors can only be code or both.

then.description: Tool to run after the strikes are used up.

max_silence_s.description: Hard ceiling on total silence regardless of inactivity nudges.

oneOf.title: Field firewall
oneOf.description: Named fields (tokens, passwords, one-time codes) are stripped from anything the LLM sees and from everything it says.
